description: What ENVO and AGROVOC say about every class the material taxonomy cites, resolved from the authorities by tools/resolve_material_anchors.py. A test compares the data files against this, so a mistyped accession -- which is a different published class that still resolves -- fails the suite offline. `parents` and `broader` are recorded because the taxonomy asserts edges the authorities do not, and the only way to keep that honest is to record what they actually say.

ENVO_00002006.label: liquid water
ENVO_00002006.definition: An environmental material primarily composed of dihydrogen oxide in its liquid form.

ENVO_00002011.label: fresh water
ENVO_00002011.definition: The lower bound of solute concentration required for water to be considered freshwater is variable, but is always less than that of seawater, and often cited as less than 1 gram of solutes per 1 litre of water.

ENVO_00002042.label: surface water
ENVO_00002042.definition: Water that is found on the surface of an astronomical object.

ENVO_04000007.label: lake water
ENVO_04000007.definition: Water which is part of a lake.

ENVO_01001004.label: groundwater
ENVO_01001004.definition: The definition of aquifer is quite permissive, referencing any water bearing rock or unconsolidated material.

ENVO_00002010.label: saline water
ENVO_00002010.definition: The threshold salt concentration for classifying water as saline varies, but typically begins at about 1,000 to 3,000 parts salt per million parts water or 0.1–0.3% salt by weight.

ENVO_00002149.label: sea water
ENVO_00002149.definition: This definition refers to water that is actually in a sea or ocean. This water may have a wide range of salinity levels.

ENVO_00003044.label: brine
ENVO_00003044.definition: It is used (now less popular than historically) to preserve vegetables, fish, and meat.

ENVO_01000600.label: rainwater
ENVO_01000600.definition: Rainwater is liquid water which has precipitated in the form of droplets through the condensation of atmospheric water vapour.

ENVO_03600002.label: cooling water
ENVO_03600002.definition: Cooling water is commonly used for cooling automobile internal combustion engines and power stations.

ENVO_00002001.label: waste water
ENVO_00002001.definition: Water that has been adversely affected in quality by anthropogenic influence.

ENVO_01000266.label: water vapour
ENVO_01000266.definition: Perhaps a better relation between water vapour and water can be found in or added to RO?

ENVO_01000268.label: atmospheric water vapour
ENVO_01000268.definition: Atmospheric water vapour is water vapour that is part of an atmosphere.

ENVO_00002012.label: hypersaline water
ENVO_00002012.definition: The average salinity of sea water is assumed to be around 35,000 ppm, equivalent to 35 grams of salt per one liter (or kilogram) of water.

ENVO_01000797.label: gaseous environmental material
ENVO_01000797.definition: A material entity which is composed of one or more chemical entities and has neither independent shape nor volume but tends to expand indefinitely.

ENVO_00005792.label: underground water
ENVO_00005792.definition: This class references any water that's under a planetary surface. For water that is in an aquifer, see "groundwater" (ENVO:01001004). Previously, this class included both.

ENVO_03605006.label: stream water
ENVO_03605006.definition: Water which is part of a stream.

c_5867fbf1.label: green water
c_5867fbf1.definition: Green water is that fraction of rainfall that infiltrates into the soil and is available to plants. It includes soil water holding capacity and the continual replenishment of reserves by rainfall.
c_5867fbf1.definition_source: Ringersma J, Batjes NH, Dent DL, 2003. Green Water: definitions and data for assessment. Report 2003/2. ISRIC – World Soil Information, Wageningen. https://edepot.wur.nl/36619
c_5867fbf1.scope_note: Green water is typically taken up by plants as evapotranspiration. Do not use this concept if referring to water with an induced density of planktonic algae.

c_b1215876.label: cooling water
c_b1215876.definition: Water which is used to absorb and remove heat. Cooling water may be broken down into water used in the generation of electricity in power stations, and cooling water used in other industrial processes.

c_6d63ccf3.label: grey water
c_6d63ccf3.definition: Wastewater from clothes, washing machines, showers, bathtubs, hand washing, lavatories and sinks. Domestic wastewater without fecal contamination, i.e., all streams except for the wastewater from toilets.
c_6d63ccf3.definition_source: Adapted from NALT https://lod.nal.usda.gov/nalt/156845 and https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greywater

c_66d531bb.label: water footprint
c_66d531bb.definition: Indicator of the total volume of fresh water that is used directly or indirectly to produce a product.
c_66d531bb.definition_source: Water for food security and nutrition, A report by the High Level Panel of Experts on Food Security and Nutrition of the Committee on World Food Security, FAO, 2015 (http://www.fao.org/3/a-av045e.pdf).
